01 · The idea

Part 1 made it work. Part 2 makes it look real.

The first four tools render, voice, subtitle and export. They make a video possible. These four fix the things that make AI videos look like AI: soft, low-res photos, cut-outs with halos, a paid voice you ration, and flat 2D where a real object should be.

The reel opens on Part 1 already installed, flips to four mystery cards, and gives each new tool its own block with its real GitHub card and a demo of the job. Part 2 joins Part 1 at the end: eight tools, $0.

02 · The setup

All four, ready to copy.

This is what you asked for in the comments. Each block installs one tool and runs it once. Or paste the last prompt into Claude Code and let it set up all four for you.

01 · real-esrgan
# Real-ESRGAN · upscale any photo ×4 (BSD-3 · github.com/xinntao/Real-ESRGAN)
# Easiest on any PC: download the portable build "realesrgan-ncnn-vulkan" from the repo's Releases page, unzip it, then:
realesrgan-ncnn-vulkan -i blurry.jpg -o sharp.png -s 4
# Faces or illustrations: add  -n realesrgan-x4plus-anime  for drawings, or keep the default for photos.
# Check the result at 200% before you use it: fine text and logos can come back invented.
02 · rembg
# rembg · cut a person or a product out of any photo (MIT · github.com/danielgatis/rembg)
pip install "rembg[cpu,cli]"
rembg i photo.jpg out.png            # one photo -> transparent PNG
rembg p ./photos ./cutouts           # a whole folder
# Hair and soft edges: try a stronger model
rembg i -m birefnet-general photo.jpg out.png
# Always check the edge on a dark AND a light background before using the cut-out.

Why these two together: upscale first, then cut out. A cut-out made from a sharp ×4 photo keeps its hair and edges; one made from a small photo looks pasted.

03 · kokoro
# Kokoro · a voice that runs on your own laptop (Apache-2.0 · github.com/hexgrad/kokoro)
pip install kokoro soundfile
# (it also needs espeak-ng installed on your system for some languages)

# voice.py
from kokoro import KPipeline
import soundfile as sf
pipe = KPipeline(lang_code='a')                 # 'a' = American English
text = "Four more tools, all free, all on your machine."
for i, (_, _, audio) in enumerate(pipe(text, voice='af_heart')):
    sf.write(f'line_{i}.wav', audio, 24000)
# No account, no API key, no credits. Try voices like af_heart, am_michael, bf_emma.

Kokoro vs ElevenLabs: ElevenLabs (Part 1) is the cloud voice with an account and credits; we still use it for the final voice. Kokoro is the free one that runs offline, perfect for drafts, tests and as many takes as you want.

04 · blender (headless)
# Blender · a 3D studio Claude runs without opening it (GPL · blender.org)
# Install Blender once from blender.org. Claude writes scene.py, then:
blender -b -P scene.py              # -b = background: no window, no clicks

# scene.py
import bpy
bpy.ops.object.select_all(action='SELECT'); bpy.ops.object.delete()
bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_uv_sphere_add(radius=1, location=(-1.2, 0, 1))
bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cube_add(size=1.6, location=(1.3, 0.4, 0.8))
bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_plane_add(size=20)
bpy.ops.object.light_add(type='AREA', location=(3, -3, 5)); bpy.context.object.data.energy = 800
bpy.ops.object.camera_add(location=(0, -7, 3), rotation=(1.2, 0, 0)); bpy.context.scene.camera = bpy.context.object
s = bpy.context.scene
s.render.resolution_x, s.render.resolution_y = 1080, 1920
s.render.filepath = '//render.png'
bpy.ops.render.render(write_still=True)
setup prompt · claude code
You are setting up my local video kit in this folder. Install and test these four free tools, one at a time,
and tell me in one line when each one works:
1. Real-ESRGAN (portable realesrgan-ncnn-vulkan): upscale test.jpg x4 to test_x4.png.
2. rembg (pip, cli): cut test.jpg out to test_cut.png; show it to me on a dark and a light background.
3. Kokoro (pip): read "This voice runs on my laptop." to test_voice.wav.
4. Blender (headless): write scene.py with a sphere, a cube, a floor, a light and a camera, run blender -b -P scene.py,
   and show me render.png.
If something fails, read the error, fix the cause (missing dependency, PATH, GPU), and retry. Never ask me to open an app.
Check 01

Look at 200%.

Upscaled text and logos can come back invented. Use the upscale for photos, not for typography.

Check 02

Dark and light.

Look at every cut-out on a dark and a light background. A halo hides on one and shouts on the other.

Check 03

One test video.

Use all four once in a 10-second test before a real reel. Fixing setup later costs more.

03 · References

Same series, new tools.

Part 2 keeps Part 1's look on purpose, so the series is recognisable: the GitHub card that types its name and rolls its stars, the Claude Code tracker filling 0/4 → 4/4, one calm background per tool, and the colour on the cards and stickers.

Real data

The four repos with their real star counts (checked on GitHub the day of the reel) and their real commands.

A demo per tool

A 48-px photo rebuilt sharp at ×4, a cut-out on a transparency checkerboard with a loupe on the edge, the real voice waveform on an offline laptop, and a 3D render filling in tiles while the app stays closed.

Calm backgrounds

Cream, soft sage, soft slate, navy, soft amber, deep green and soft sky: the backgrounds stay quiet so the colour lives on top.

04 · Claude session

How this reel was made.

What came back: Part 1's project copied as the base, a block-by-block brief, the narration with 125 time-stamped words, and two builders working at the same time: one on the hook, the tracker and the ending, the other on the four tool demos.

The reviews that changed it: the first cut was clear but small and quiet, so the demos got bigger, every stressed word got a sticker, and the Kokoro block now shows why a second voice tool: paid cloud voice vs free local voice. When the colours went too loud, the backgrounds went back to calm tones and the colour moved onto the cards.

What came back: 47.5 seconds at 1080×1920 and 30 fps, 14 Mbps, the voice plus 71 sound effects on real events, mixed at −14 LUFS.

06 · Decisions

Where the taste is.

01

A series, on purpose

Part 1 was our most-watched edu. Part 2 keeps its format so people who saw it recognise it in one second.

02

Say why the overlap

Kokoro and ElevenLabs are both voices. The reel shows the difference (paid cloud vs free local) instead of leaving it to guess.

03

Show the job, not the logo

No tool logos: each one is shown doing its job on a real image, sound or scene.

04

Colour on top, calm behind

Contrast comes from coloured cards and stickers on quiet backgrounds, never from loud floods that steal the eye.
